title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court Concerning Whether to Permit Foreign Litigants to Appoint as Their Litigation Agents Foreigners Residing in China or Staff of Their Country's Consulate in China

articles.content_en: 1. Where a foreign party entrusts a national of his/her own country residing within the territory of China to act as a litigation agent, and such entrustment does not contravene the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), it may be permitted.

2. When an official of a foreign embassy or consulate in China, entrusted by a national of his/her own country, acts as a litigation agent in a personal capacity, such action shall also be permitted. At the same time, in accordance with the provisions of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations to which China has acceded, a consular official of a foreign embassy in China (including a diplomat of a foreign embassy in China who concurrently holds a consular title as confirmed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China) may, when the national of his/her own country who is a party is not within the territory of China or, for other reasons, cannot appear before a Chinese court in a timely manner, directly act as a representative in the name of the consular office, or arrange for a representative to appear before a Chinese court on behalf of such national, even without a formal entrustment.

With respect to the issue raised in your request for instructions concerning Jutta Maurer, a national of the Federal Republic of Germany who originally resided in China and, after returning to her home country, intends to entrust a national of her own country who is teaching in Shanghai or a staff member of the Consulate of her country in Shanghai to act as her agent in her divorce action, the foregoing opinion may be referred to for handling.

This is a reply.
